holidays.name: National Comic Book Day
holidays.description: Grab a stack of your favorite issues and settle in with some superheroes, villains, or indie oddities. Comic fans use the day to flip through old favorites, hunt through dusty back-issue bins, and introduce a friend to the joys of panels and speech bubbles.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite date for comic shops, collectors, and fans to celebrate the art form.
holidays.funFact: Comics are collected like fine art. Rare copies of early superhero issues have sold for millions of dollars at auction.

holidays.name: National One-Hit Wonder Day
holidays.description: Time to blast the songs from artists who struck chart gold exactly once and then vanished into trivia-night legend. Build a playlist of catchy earworms and see how many of the singers' names you can remember.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with music lovers who enjoy giving one-time chart-toppers a victory lap.
holidays.funFact: Many one-hit wonders are still instantly recognizable decades later. Their songs often outlive the careers of the artists who made them, thanks to movies, commercials, and wedding dance floors.

holidays.name: National Lobster Day
holidays.description: Crack out the bibs and melted butter. This day honors the red-shelled crustacean, whether it shows up as a lobster roll, a steamed whole lobster, or a bowl of bisque.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is celebrated by seafood lovers and restaurants, especially in coastal regions.
holidays.funFact: Lobsters were once considered so common in colonial New England that they were fed to prisoners and servants. Today they are a symbol of fancy dining.
